By this they meant His words ﴿If We will, We shall cause the earth to swallow them, or cause pieces of the sky to fall upon them﴾ [Saba' 9], and His words ﴿And if they see a piece of the sky falling, they would say: "A gathered cloud"﴾ [al-Tur 44], since it is a threat to them with the portents of the Hour and their standing before reckoning. They took "min" in His words ﴿kisfan min al-sama'﴾ [al-Tur 44] as partitive, meaning a fragment of the celestial bodies; therefore they refused to make the verb "tusqita" transitive to the substance of the sky itself. Know that this requires that these two verses, or one of them, were revealed before Surat al-Isra'; and that is not unlikely.

Kisaf (with kasra on the kaf and fatha on the sin) is the plural of kisfa, a piece of a thing, like sidra and sidar. Nafi', Ibn 'Amir, Abu Bakr from 'Asim, and Abu Ja'far read it so; the rest read it with a sukun on the sin, in the sense of the passive participle, i.e., "maksuf," meaning "maqtu'" (cut).

[p. 209]
Al-za'm: a statement that is far-fetched or impossible.

Al-qabil: a group of one kind. It is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal) of "al-malaika," meaning they are a particular unfamiliar group, as though they said: "or you bring a company of the kind of the angels."

Al-zukhruf: gold.

The verb "turqa" was given the locative particle "fi" (in) to indicate that ascent is a gradual progression through the heavens, like one who climbs a ladder or staircase.

Then they became inventive in their proposals and asked him, if he ascended, to send down to them a book from the sky which they could read, containing testimony that he had reached the sky. It is said the one who said this was 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Umayya, who said: "until you bring us a book with you, with four angels testifying for you."

Perhaps they meant that a complete book should descend upon them from the sky all at once, so that they would be denying the gradual revelation of the Qur'an, supposing that its being revealed in portions does not suit its being sent down from God; for gradual revelation, in their view, implies deliberation and contrivance in its composition. For this reason the Qur'an often explains the wisdom of its gradual revelation.

The lam in His words ﴿li-ruqiyyika﴾ may be the lam of specification, with "ruqiyyika" as the object of "nu'minu," like His statement ﴿we will never believe you﴾; so the claim of ascent is denied of him as something they would not affirm until a book descends upon them. It may also be the lam of cause, with the object of "nu'mina" omitted, indicated by His preceding words ﴿we will never believe you﴾, the sense being: "we will never affirm you because of your ascent," namely "that You send down to us a book." The meaning is that if he ascended into the sky, they would disbelieve their own eyes until he sent them a book they could see descending from the sky; and this is a sneer and mockery on their part.

Since their proposal was one of obstinate contention and stubbornness, God commanded him to answer them in a way that expresses wonder at their words with the phrase ﴿Glory be to my Lord!﴾, which is used to express wonder, as was mentioned at the opening of this surah; then with a rhetorical interrogative and the exclusive construction that restricts himself to humanity and messengership, a restriction relative to what they claim (i.e., I am not a lord who disposes of affairs and creates what is demanded of me); so how could I bring God and the angels? And how could I create on earth what has not been created in it?

The majority read "qul" (say) in the imperative form. Ibn Kathir and Ibn 'Amir read "qala" (he said) with an alif after the qaf, in the past tense, as a report of the Messenger's ﷺ answer to their statement ﴿We will never believe you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth﴾, in the manner of iltifat (shift of grammatical person).

Commentary of Ibn 'Ashur (al-Tahrir wa al-Tanwir) on surah 17, verses 94–95:

﴿And nothing prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them, except that they said: "Has Allah sent a mere human as a messenger?"﴾ ﴿Say: "If there were angels walking calmly on the earth, We would have sent down to them from the heaven an angel as a messenger."﴾.

After the forms of their obstinacy and the manifestations of their denial had been enumerated, there follows the explanation of the fundamental cause that prompts denial among all nations, namely their presumption that it is impossible for Allah to send to people a message through one of their own kind, a human like them. This presumption is the source of the excuses they make. Those whose basic belief is this, there is no hope that they will believe, even if every sign came to them. The purpose of their various proposals is nothing but to satisfy their illusions and to evade entering the religion. Had the Messenger brought them what they asked for, they would have turned and said: "That is indeed sorcery," or "Our hearts are covered," or something similar. Along with this explanation of the root of their disbelief, it is also a specific refutation of their saying ﴿Or you bring Allah and the angels before us as a guarantee﴾ [al-Isra: 92], and a refutation of their saying ﴿Or you ascend into the heaven﴾ [al-Isra: 93], and so on to the end.

Page 212
His saying ﴿except that they said: "Has Allah sent a mere human as a messenger?"﴾ explicitly indicates that they uttered it with their tongues, and it is also, along with that, a metonymy for their belief in what they said. For this reason He made their saying that a barrier to their believing, because the belief of those who say it prevents their believing in its opposite, and their uttering what they believe prevents those who hear them from among the followers of their religion.
The delivery of this statement in the form of restriction (ḥaṣr) and the particle of generality made it a conclusion (tadhyīl) to what preceded of the account of their varied methods of denial and mockery.

The apparent reading is to take the definite article in "al-nās" (the people) as covering all (istighrāq), meaning: nothing prevented all people from believing except that false presumption. This is because Allah related the same from every nation that denied its messenger, saying, relating about the people of Noah: ﴿This is only a human like you who wants to make himself superior over you. Had Allah willed, He would have sent down angels. We have not heard of this among our forefathers of old﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 24].

The same is related about Hud: ﴿This is only a human like you, who eats of what you eat and drinks of what you drink. And if you obey a human like yourselves, then you are indeed losers﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 33]; and about the people of Salih: ﴿You are only a human like us﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 154]; and about the people of Shu'ayb: ﴿And you are only a human like us﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 186]; and it is related about the people of Pharaoh: ﴿They said: "Shall we believe in two humans like ourselves?"﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 47]; and the people of Muhammad (ﷺ) said: ﴿But they wonder that a warner has come to them from among themselves, and the disbelievers say, "This is a strange thing."﴾ [Qaf: 2]. If the generality includes the disbelievers of Quraysh, the Messenger was commanded to answer this doubt with His saying ﴿If there were angels walking calmly on the earth﴾ and the verse to its end. Thus Allah singled out His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) to uproot this doubt from its origin, a singling out not granted to any of the earlier messengers, for they met that doubt by seeking Allah's help against their opponents. So He said of Noah: ﴿He said: "My Lord, my people have denied me. So judge between me and them with a decisive judgment, and save me and those who are with me of the believers"﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 117].

Page 213
He said the same about Hud and Salih, and He said about Musa and Harun: ﴿So they denied them, and they were among those destroyed﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 48]. Allah has thus reserved for His Messenger decisive proofs to nullify polytheism and the doubts of misguidance, in a manner suited to his being the Seal of the Messengers. For this reason he said in the sermon of the Farewell Pilgrimage: "Indeed, Satan has despaired of being worshipped in this land of yours, but he has been content to be obeyed in matters other than that, of the deeds you consider trivial."

The meaning of His saying ﴿If there were angels walking on the earth﴾ etc. is that Allah sends the Messenger to a people from their own kind, so that association is possible, for unity of kind is the foundation of ease of companionship. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And if We had made him an angel, We would have made him a man﴾ [al-An'am: 9], i.e., in the form of a man so that communication between him and people is possible.

The clause "yamshūna" (walking) is a descriptive clause (waṣf) for "malā'ika" (angels).

"Muṭma'innīn" is a circumstantial qualifier (ḥāl). The muṭma'inn is the one at rest, and what is meant here is the one who is settled and not agitated, i.e., walking in a manner of settled residence on the earth. The meaning is: if there were angels dwelling on the earth, not descending with a message for the messengers, We would have sent down to them an angel.

Since walking and being at rest on the earth are attributes of humans, the meaning reverts to: if you were angels, We would have sent down to you an angel from the heaven. Since you are humans, We sent to you a human like you. The coming of guidance is the call of the messengers to guidance.

﴿قُلْ كَفى بِاللَّهِ شَهِيدًا بَيْنِي وبَيْنَكم إنَّهُ كانَ بِعِبادِهِ خَبِيرًا بَصِيرًا﴾ [Say: "Allah suffices as a witness between me and you. Indeed, He is ever Acquainted and Seeing with His servants."]

After Allah had specially granted Muhammad ﷺ the decisive argument against misguidance, He followed that by instructing him in what He had taught the earlier messengers: entrusting the matter to Allah and leaving the judgment against his enemies to Him. So He commanded him, ﴿Say: "Allah suffices"﴾, as consolation for him, as strengthening for his own soul, and as an assurance that He would decide between him and them. This is like what Nuh and Hud said, ﴿My Lord, help me, for they have denied me﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 26], and what other messengers said, close to this.

This also constitutes a rejection, in summary, of all their earlier proposals taken together.

The object of "kafa" (sufficed) is omitted; its implied form is "kafani" (sufficed me). "Al-shahid" (the witness) means "al-shahid" in the sense of one who informs about a matter exactly as it happened.

Here "al-shahid" is intended to mean the one who bears witness for the righteous against the wrongdoer. It is thus a metonymy (kinaya) for the helper and the judge, because testimony is the cause of judgment. The indicator (qarina) is His saying ﴿between me and you﴾, since the adverbial expression "bayn" (between) suits the meaning of judgment. This has the same sense as His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Until Allah judges between us, and He is the best of judges﴾ [al-A'raf: 87], and His saying ﴿On the Day of Resurrection He will separate between you﴾ [al-Mumtahanah: 3].

The "ba'" (bi-) attached to the Name of Allah is redundant (za'idah), serving to emphasize the attachment of the verb "kafa" to its subject. Its original form is: "Allah suffices as a witness."

The clause ﴿Indeed, He is ever Acquainted and Seeing with His servants﴾ gives the reason for being content with Allah alone. "Al-khabir" (the Acquainted) means the All-Knowing, and it is intended to mean the One who knows intentions and realities. "Al-basir" (the Seeing) means the All-Knowing of essences and of what is observed of their conditions. The purpose of following the one with the other is the comprehensiveness and all-encompassing nature of His knowledge.

Commentary of Ibn 'Ashur (al-Tahrir wa al-Tanwir) on surah 17, verse 97:

﴿And whomever Allah guides, he is the one guided; and whomever He leaves astray, you will not find for them allies besides Him.﴾ It is possible that this sentence is conjoined to the sentence ﴿And what prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them﴾ [al-Isra: 94], combining the apparent, customary obstacle to guidance with the true obstacle, which is the withholding of divine success (tawfiq) from Allah, exalted is He. Thus, whoever persists in disbelief despite the clarity of the proof for people of intellect, that is because Allah, exalted is He, has not granted him success. The causes of this deprivation are the anger of Allah toward one who does not submit his intellect to receive the truth and takes his desire as his guide in matters of earnestness.

It is also possible that the sentence is conjoined to the sentence ﴿Say: Allah suffices as a witness between me and you﴾ [al-Isra: 96], as an escalation in consolation, meaning: do not let their failure to be guided grieve you, for Allah has deprived them of being guided because they adopted obstinacy before reflecting on the reality of the message.

The guidance here means guidance to belief in what the Messenger ﷺ brought.

The definite article in "al-muhtadi" (the one guided) is the definite article of mental reference (ta'rif al-'ahd al-dhihni, the definiteness of a known but mentally referenced thing), so the defined term is equivalent to the indefinite. It is as if it were said: "then he is guided." The benefit of predicating guidance of him is to prepare for the mention of its opposite, namely ﴿and whomever He leaves astray, you will not find for them allies﴾, just as one says: "Whoever knows me, knows me; and whoever does not know me, I am so-and-so."

It is also possible to take the definite article in His saying ﴿then he is the one guided﴾ as the definite article of the genus (ta'rif al-jins). It then conveys a restriction (qasr) of guidance to the one whom Allah guides, a restriction of relation (qasr idafi), meaning: not the one whom you wish to guide, and whom Allah has led astray. It cannot be understood as a restriction of claim (qasr idda'i) that carries the meaning of perfection, because the guidance intended here is a single guidance, namely guidance to belief.

The letter yā' of "al-muhtadi" was omitted in the orthography of the Mushaf, because they stopped on it without the yā', according to the dialect of those who pause on a defective noun that is not tanwinated by dropping the yā'. This is an eloquent dialect, not analogous to the standard rule, but it was preferred for lightness, given the heaviness of the form of the active participle together with the weakness of the weak letter at the end of the word. It was written without yā' because the rule for word endings is that they are written with regard to the state of pause. As for pronunciation in continuous recitation (wasl), Nafi' and Abu 'Amr recited it with the yā' in continuous recitation, and this is the preferred form. For this reason, they wrote the yā' in their Mushafs in red ink and made it finer than the rest of the letters written in the Mushaf, to distinguish it from what the Companions, the scribes of the Mushaf, had written. The others dropped the yā' in pronunciation during continuous recitation, treating continuous recitation like pause. Although this is rare outside poetry, eloquent speakers treat the fawasil (verse-endings) like rhyme (qawafi), and they regarded the fasila as every sentence with which speech is completed, as Sibawayh's illustration of writing the fasila indicates, with His saying ﴿By the night when it passes﴾ [al-Fajr: 4] and His saying ﴿He said: that is what we were seeking﴾ [al-Kahf: 64]. Something of this has already been mentioned under His saying ﴿Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Great, the Exalted﴾ [al-Ra'd: 9] in surah al-Ra'd.

The address in ﴿then you will not find for them allies besides Him﴾ is to the Prophet ﷺ, because this statement is intended to console him over their failure to respond to him. Thus, the negation of finding allies is a metonymy (kinaya) for the negation of allies existing for them, because if they existed he would have found them and known them.

The allies (awliya') are the helpers, meaning: you will not find for them helpers who rescue them from the consequence of misguidance, which is the punishment. It is also possible that "awliya'" means those who manage their affairs, meaning: you will not find for them anyone who sets their condition right by bringing them out of misguidance, as in His saying ﴿Allah is the ally of those who believe; He brings them out of darkness into light﴾ [al-Baqarah: 257].

The plural "awliya'" is used in view of the correspondence of plural to plural, meaning: you will not find for each one of them an ally, nor for their group an ally, as one says: "The people mounted their animals."

"Min dunihi" means: other than Him.

* * *

﴿And We will gather them on the Day of Resurrection upon their faces, blind, mute, and deaf; their refuge is Hell; whenever it subsides, We increase for them the blaze.﴾

He mentions the purpose of the negation of an ally, or of their being given a refuge, by mentioning the form of their punishment in His saying ﴿And We will gather them on the Day of Resurrection upon their faces﴾, and so on.

[Page 217]

Gathering (hashr) is the bringing together of people from scattered places to one place. Since this requires their walking, the verb "hashr" is followed by the preposition "'ala" (upon), by implicit meaning of the verb "yamshun" (they walk). People understood this from the verse and asked the Prophet ﷺ: "How will they walk upon their faces?" He said: "The One who made them walk upon their feet is able to make them walk upon their faces."

The purpose of this is to combine disfigurement and punishment, because the face is less able to bear the hardness of the ground than the foot.

This is a fitting recompense for the crime, because they presented misguidance in the form of truth and branded truth with the marks of misguidance. So their recompense was that their faces were turned into organs of walking instead of their feet. Then they were ﴿blind and mute﴾ as recompense for their false words against the Messenger and against the Qur'an, and deaf as recompense for their refusal to hear the truth, as He said about them: ﴿And they say: our hearts are in coverings against what you call us to, and in our ears is deafness, and between us and you is a barrier﴾ [Fussilat: 5]. And He said about them: ﴿He said: My Lord, why have You gathered me blind, when I was seeing? He said: Thus Our signs came to you and you forgot them, and thus today you are forgotten﴾ [Ta-Ha: 125]. And He said about them: ﴿And whoever is blind in this world, he will be blind in the Hereafter﴾ [al-Isra: 72], meaning: whoever was blind to the truth will, at the gathering, be deprived of the pleasure of sight. This is their state at the gathering.

"Al-ma'wa" is the place of refuge (mahall al-awy), that is, of settling in a refuge, meaning the abode and the dwelling place.

"Khabat al-nar" (the fire subsided), with khubuw and khab', means its flame decreased.

"Al-sa'ir" is the flame of the fire. It is derived from "sa'r al-nar," when its fuel is stirred up. The adjective is masculine in agreement with the masculine gender of "al-lahab" (the flame), and the meaning is: We increase them in flame within it.

In His saying ﴿whenever it subsides, We increase for them the blaze﴾ there is a difficulty, because the fire of Hell does not subside, and Allah has said ﴿so the punishment will not be lightened for them﴾ [al-Baqarah: 86]. On the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, the disbelievers are the fuel of the fire, as He said: ﴿Its fuel is people and stones﴾ [al-Baqarah: 24]. So when the fire burns them, the flame that was rising from their bodies disappears, and they are not long before they are returned as they were, so the blaze returns to them.

[Page 218]

Thus the subsiding and increase of the blaze is in relation to their bodies, not to the essence of the fire of Hell. For this subtle point, the verb "zidnahum" (We increased them) was directed at the pronoun of the polytheists, to indicate that the increase of the blaze occurs in them. It is as if it were said: "whenever it subsides in them, We increase them in blaze," and it was not said: "We increase it in blaze."

In my view, the meaning of the verse proceeds by way of mockery (tahakkum) and of raising hopes that end in disappointment, because it made the increase of the blaze accompany every time of subsiding, as the word "kullama" (whenever), which means every time, indicates. Outwardly this is an encouragement of a subsiding occurring, because the word "khabw" appears outwardly, but it ends in despair of it, since it indicates the perpetuity of its blaze at all times, by the association of the increase of its blaze with every time of its subsiding. So this statement belongs to the category of allusive wit (tamlih), of the same kind as His saying ﴿And they will not enter Paradise until the camel passes through the eye of the needle﴾ [al-A'raf: 40], and the words of Iyas the judge to the adversary who asked him: "Against whom did you rule?" He said: "Against the son of your maternal aunt."

**Commentary of Ibn 'Ashur (al-Tahrir wa al-Tanwir) on surah 17, verse 98:**

﴿That is their recompense, because they disbelieved in Our signs and said, "When we are bones and crumbled dust, will we indeed be resurrected in a new creation?"﴾

This is an *istinaf bayani* (an explanatory resumptive clause), because the dreadful punishment just described prompts the listeners to ask about the reason this severe form of retribution has been assembled. The answer is that it is due to their disbelief in the signs and their denial of the return (al-ma'ad).

The reference back to what came before, namely His words ﴿And We shall gather them on the Day of Resurrection upon their faces﴾ [al-Isra: 97] up to the end of that verse, is interpreted as "the aforementioned."

*Al-jaza'* (recompense) means the return given in exchange for an action.

The *ba'* in ﴿because they disbelieved﴾ (*bi-annahum kafaru*) indicates causation (*sababiyyah*).

[Page 219]

It is apparent that the sentence ﴿and they said, "When we are bones…"﴾ (*wa qalu a-idha kunna 'izaman*) and so on, is coordinated (*'atf*) with the sentence ﴿because they disbelieved﴾. Thus the text mentions the reason these punishments are gathered together for them, and it mentions two causes:

The first is their disbelief in the signs. This includes various kinds of crimes, both in detail and in summary, and the punishment in His words ﴿And We shall gather them on the Day of Resurrection upon their faces, blind, mute, and deaf; their abode is Hell﴾ [al-Isra: 97] is suited to them.

The second is their denial of resurrection, expressed in their words ﴿When we are bones and crumbled dust, will we indeed be resurrected in a new creation?﴾. It is fitting for them to be punished with a punishment that corresponds to what they denied, namely the renewal of life after they have become crumbled dust, for the crumbling by burning is more complete in its dissolution than the crumbling of bones in the dust.

The interrogative in the quotation of their words ﴿When we are bones…﴾ and in His words ﴿will we indeed be resurrected…﴾ is a denial (*inkari*). The disagreement among the Qur'an readers (*qurra'*) has already been discussed regarding the retention of the two hamzas in the phrase *a-idha* (أئِذا), and regarding their retention in the phrase *a-inna* (أإنّا) in His words ﴿will we indeed be resurrected﴾, in the parallel verse in this surah.

The sentence ﴿Do they not see that God, who created the heavens and the earth, is able to create their like, and has appointed for them a term about which there is no doubt? Yet the wrongdoers refuse anything but disbelief.﴾ is a continuation of the sentence ﴿That is their recompense﴾ [al-Isra: 98], in view of what the preceding sentence contains of deterrence against their saying ﴿When we are bones and crumbled dust, shall we really be raised up as a new creation?﴾ [al-Isra: 98]. After rebuking them with a threat for denying resurrection, it adds a refutation of their belief by way of argument from analogy (qiyas al-tamthil, analogy by similitude) concerning possibility. This is sufficient to convince them here, because they denied resurrection only on the belief that it is impossible, as their speech expressed through the rhetorical question of denial shows, and their judgement of impossibility rests on the fact that they have become bones and crumbled dust, meaning that the creation of the likes of those parts is beyond reach. They did not offer any other proof. Thus the analogy of creating bodies from decayed parts with the creation of things greater than them from non-existence, which is further removed from annihilation, is a proof that cuts off their claim.

The interrogative in ﴿Did they not see﴾ is a denial mixed with wonder at the absence of their knowledge. Since their beliefs were grounded in deeming resurrection unlikely, they were in the state of one to whom the signs of God's power have not become apparent, so the statement comes to affirm that they in fact knew this in reality.

The verb "to see" (ra'a) is used in the sense of belief, since it is followed by a clause on God being able, and that is not something perceived by the eyes. The meaning is: ﴿Did they not know that God is able to create their like?﴾

The pronoun in "their like" refers back to what the pronoun in "they see" refers to, namely the people in His words ﴿and what prevented the people﴾ [al-Isra: 94], meaning the polytheists.

"Mithl" (like) means the one resembling, i.e., He is able to create people resembling them, because the discussion concerns establishing the re-creation of the bodies of those who denied it, not that God is able to create some other creation. The verse implies that resurrection is the re-creation of other bodies from non-existence, so that for every dead person a new body is created in the likeness of his body that existed in this world, and into it is placed the soul that belonged to him.

It is also possible that the word "mithl" here is a kinaya (metonymy) for the very thing it is attached to, as in the Arabic saying "your like does not stint," and in His words ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾ [al-Shura: 11] according to one of its two interpretations, namely by treating the kaf attached to "mithlihi" as not superfluous. The meaning would then be: ﴿He is able to create them,﴾ that is, to bring back their creation, for that is no more wondrous than the creation of the heavens and the earth.

Our scholars have various approaches to the re-creation of bodies at resurrection. It was said that the re-creation is from non-existence. It was said that it is from all the scattered parts of the bodies. It was said that from the "ajb al-dhanab" (the coccyx) of each person a new body grows, similar to his body, just as a tree grows from a date-stone resembling the tree that bore the fruit of that stone.

The description of the Name of Majesty (Allah) by a relative clause (alladhi khalaqa) is to indicate the basis on which the predicate is constructed, namely the denial directed at them, because the creation of the heavens and the earth is a matter that is observed and known, and that it is the act of God is something they do not dispute.

The clause ﴿and has appointed for them a term about which there is no doubt﴾ is conjoined to the clause "Did they not see," because it is taken to mean: they have seen this, had they had minds; that is, they should have realised that God is able to re-create creation, and He has appointed for them a term about which there is no doubt.

The ajal (term) is a time set as a limit that is reached in some state, and its use became common for the span of life, which is the period determined for every living thing according to what God has placed in it of soundness of bodily faculties and what He knows of the accidents that befall it, which cut into some of that soundness or strengthen it.

The ajal here may be understood as the time appointed for the occurrence of resurrection in God's knowledge.

The reason why this appointing (al-ja'l) is for them is that they are among those who are included in that term, since they are among those who will be raised at that time. Their being singled out with mention is because they are the ones who denied resurrection. The meaning is: and He has appointed a term for them and for others.

The meaning of the term being one about which there is no doubt is that there ought not to be any doubt about it, and that the doubt of those who doubt is obstinacy or turning away from reflection. It is thus of the same kind as His words ﴿This is the Book, there is no doubt in it﴾ [al-Baqara: 2].

It is also possible that the term is the term of life, that is, a term has been appointed for their lives. This would be a second argument for resurrection, meaning: did they not see that He has appointed a term for their lives? Then He who brought them into being and gave them life, and appointed a term for their lives, did so only because He will return them to another life; otherwise He would not cause them to perish after having given them life. For wisdom requires that what the Wise One brings into existence He keeps in being and preserves from perishing. Therefore this perishing about which there is no doubt is only a passing annihilation, in preparation for an existence greater and more lasting than this existence.

On this reading, the reason why this appointing is for them is evident, because the terms are their terms, and that it is about which there is no doubt is also evident, because they do not doubt that their lives have terms. The words ﴿and has appointed for them a term﴾ carry an allusion, on both meanings, to the favour of the respite as a blessing, and an allusion to reminding them of the outpouring of provisions upon them during the period of the term, because mention of the creation of the heaven and the earth is a reminder of what the heavens and the earth contain of provisions and their causes.

The clause ﴿yet the wrongdoers refuse anything but disbelief﴾ is a consequence of the two clauses, in view of what they contain of denial and wonder. That is: they knew that He who created the heavens and the earth is able to re-create bodies, and yet, despite their knowledge, they refused anything but disbelief. The consequence is therefore part of the denial against them and of the wonder at their condition.

The exception of disbelief from refusal is an emphasis of a thing by means of what resembles its opposite.

Kufur (disbelief) is the denial of a blessing, and it was mentioned earlier. Disbelief was chosen here to draw attention to the fact that they disbelieved in what must be believed, and disbelieved the blessing of the Benefactor upon them, so they worshipped other than the Benefactor.

Commentary of Ibn 'Ashur (al-Tahrir wa al-Tanwir) on surah 17, verse 100:

﴿Say: "Even if you possessed the treasures of the mercy of my Lord, you would surely withhold them for fear of spending. And man has ever been tight-fisted."﴾ This is an interjected statement (i'tiraD), arising from some of their proposals, which they imagined would not be fulfilled, as evidence for the denial of the sending of a bringer of good news. So the discourse is a resumption (isti'naf) to complete the refutation of their doubts. This is a response to what their saying contained, ﴿until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth﴾ [al-Isra: 90] up to His saying "gushing forth" (tafjiran), and their saying ﴿or you have a house of gold﴾ [al-Isra: 93], from the impossibility of that occurring, because of its great value.

The meaning of the response: this is not great in comparison with the treasures of God's mercy, if He wished to manifest it for you.

Incorporated (udmija) into this response is a clarification of their stinginess in spending in the way of good. Also incorporated into this is a reminder to them that God gave them from the treasures of His mercy, yet they disbelieved His blessing and thanked the idols, which have no blessing. It is suitable that this be an address to all people, believers and disbelievers alike, each according to his share.

The usual pattern of (law) is that the verb follows it, in the past tense most often, or in the present tense in certain considerations. It is specifically followed by verbs. If they place a noun after it in speech and delay the verb after the noun, they do so for an eloquent purpose: either for the purpose of emphasis and affirmation, to indicate that mentioning the verb after the particle, then mentioning its subject, then mentioning the verb a second time, is emphasis and reinforcement, like His saying ﴿And if one of the polytheists seeks your protection﴾ [al-Tawbah: 6]. Or it is for the transition from emphasis to restriction (ikhtisas), on the basis that the subject was only moved from its place for the purpose of a path not trodden. This consideration is the one by which the analysis of this verse and similar eloquent speech is required, and among it is the saying of 'Umar to Abu 'Ubaydah: "Had anyone other than you said it..."

The meaning: even if you were singled out with ownership of the treasures of God's mercy, apart from God, you would not spend anything on the poor. That is more severe in rebuke, and in showing favour by imagining that the bounty of another is as nothing.

Both considerations do not contradict the restriction of (law) to verbs, since it suffices that the verb occurs within its scope without directly following it. Its direct following is the more common case. However, it is not permitted to say: "Had you been knowledgeable, you would have surpassed the peers."

The present-tense verb was chosen, because the intention is to suppose that they possess that in the future.

"You would have withheld" (amsaktum) here is treated as intransitive, so no object is assumed for it, because the intended meaning is: "then you would have been characterized by withholding," i.e. stinginess. One says: "So-and-so is mumsik," meaning stingy, and it is not intended that he is withholding some specific thing.

The answer of (law) is emphasized by the addition of the particle (idhan) in it, to strengthen the sense of being an answer, and because (idhan) carries the meaning of a condition, as was mentioned just before at His saying ﴿Say: "If there were with Him other gods, as you say, they would certainly have sought a way to the Lord of the Throne."﴾ [al-Isra: 42]. From this is the saying of Bishr ibn 'Awanah:

O Fatimah, had you witnessed in the bottom of Khabt, when the lion (hizbr) met your brother Bishr,
Then you would have seen a lion, or rather a lion, a mighty hizbr meeting a hizbr.

The clause ﴿and man has ever been tight-fisted﴾ is either a circumstantial clause (hal) or a parenthetical clause at the end of the speech. It gives a concluding generalization (tadhyil), because its ruling is general. Therefore the waw in it is not a conjunction.

The qatur (tight-fisted) is one who is extremely stingy, derived from (al-qatr), which is constriction in spending.

بَقِيَ قَوْلُهم ﴿أوْ تُسْقِطَ السَّماءَ كَما زَعَمْتَ عَلَيْنا كِسَفًا﴾ [al-Isra': 92] غَيْرَ مَرْدُودٍ عَلَيْهِمْ؛ لِأنَّ لَهُ مُخالَفَةً لِبَقِيَّةِ ما اقْتَرَحُوهُ بِأنَّهُ اقْتِراحُ آيَةِ عَذابٍ ورُعْبٍ، فَهو مِن قَبِيلِ آياتِ مُوسى عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ التِّسْعِ، فَكانَ ذِكْرُ ما آتاهُ اللَّهُ مُوسى مِنَ الآياتِ، وعَدَمِ إجْداءِ ذَلِكَ في فِرْعَوْنَ وقَوْمِهِ تَنْظِيرًا لِما سَألَهُ المُشْرِكُونَ.

وَالمَقْصُودُ: أنَّنا آتَيْنا مُوسى عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ تِسْعَ آياتٍ بَيِّناتِ الدَّلالَةِ عَلى صِدْقِهِ، فَلَمْ يَهْتَدِ فِرْعَوْنُ وقَوْمُهُ، وزَعَمُوا ذَلِكَ سِحْرًا، فَفي ذَلِكَ

[صفحة ٢٢٥]
مَثَلٌ لِلْمُكابِرِينَ كُلِّهِمْ، وما قُرَيْشٌ إلّا مِنهم، فَفي هَذا مَثَلٌ لِلْمُعانِدِينَ وتَسْلِيَةٌ لِلرَّسُولِ. والآياتُ التِّسْعُ هي: بَياضُ يَدِهِ كُلَّما أدْخَلَها في جَيْبِهِ وأخْرَجَها، وانْقِلابُ العَصا حَيَّةً، والطُّوفانُ، والجَرادُ، والقَمْلُ، والضَّفادِعُ، والدَّمُ، والرِّجْزُ وهو الدُّمَّلُ، والقَحْطُ وهو السُّنُونَ ونَقْصُ الثَّمَراتِ. وهي مَذْكُورَةٌ في سُورَةِ الأعْرافِ، وجَمَعَها الفَيْرُوزَ آبادِيُّ في قَوْلِهِ:

عَصًا سَنَةٌ بَحْرٌ جَرادٌ وقُمَّلُ يَدٌ ودَمٌ بَعْدَ الضَّفادِعِ طُوفانُ

(أي: العصا، والسنة [القحط]، والبحر [الماء]، والجراد، والقمل، واليد، والدم، ثم الضفادع، والطوفان.)

فَقَدْ حَصَلَتْ بِقَوْلِهِ ﴿ولَقَدْ آتَيْنا مُوسى تِسْعَ آياتٍ بَيِّناتٍ﴾ الحُجَّةُ عَلى المُشْرِكِينَ الَّذِينَ يَقْتَرِحُونَ الآياتِ.

ثُمَّ لَمْ يَزَلِ الِاعْتِناءُ في هَذِهِ السُّورَةِ بِالمُقارَنَةِ بَيْنَ رِسالَةِ مُحَمَّدٍ ﷺ، ورِسالَةِ مُوسى عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ، إقامَةً لِلْحُجَّةِ عَلى المُشْرِكِينَ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِالرِّسالَةِ بِعِلَّةِ أنَّ الَّذِي جاءَهم بَشَرٌ، ولِلْحُجَّةِ عَلى أهْلِ الكِتابِ الَّذِينَ ظاهَرُوا المُشْرِكِينَ، ولَقَّنُوهم شُبَهَ الإلْحادِ في الرِّسالَةِ المُحَمَّدِيَّةِ؛ لِيَصْفُوَ لَهم جَوُّ العِلْمِ في بِلادِ العَرَبِ، وهم ما كانُوا يَحْسُبُونَ لِما وراءَ ذَلِكَ حِسابًا.

فالمَعْنى: ولَقَدْ آتَيْنا مُوسى تِسْعَ آياتٍ عَلى رِسالَتِهِ.

وهَذا مِثْلُ التَّنْظِيرِ بَيْنَ إيتاءِ مُوسى، وإيتاءِ القُرْآنِ، في قَوْلِهِ في أوَّلِ السُّورَةِ ﴿وآتَيْنا مُوسى الكِتابَ﴾ [al-Isra': 2] الآياتِ، ثُمَّ قَوْلِهِ ﴿إنَّ هَذا القُرْآنَ يَهْدِي لِلَّتِي هي أقْوَمُ﴾ [al-Isra': 9].

فَتَكُونُ هَذِهِ الجُمْلَةُ عَطْفًا عَلى جُمْلَةِ ﴿قُلْ سُبْحانَ رَبِّي هَلْ كُنْتُ إلّا بَشَرًا رَسُولًا﴾ [al-Isra': 93] أوْ عَلى جُمْلَةِ ﴿قُلْ لَوْ أنْتُمْ تَمْلِكُونَ خَزائِنَ رَحْمَةِ رَبِّي﴾ [al-Isra': 100] الآيَةَ، ثُمَّ انْتَقَلَ مِن ذَلِكَ بِطَرِيقَةِ التَّفْرِيعِ إلى التَّسْجِيلِ بِبَنِي إسْرائِيلَ؛ اسْتِشْهادًا بِهِمْ عَلى المُشْرِكِينَ، وإدْماجًا لِلتَّعْرِيضِ بِهِمْ بِأنَّهم ساوَوُا المُشْرِكِينَ في إنْكارِ

[صفحة ٢٢٦]
نُبُوَّةِ مُحَمَّدٍ ﷺ، ومُظاهَرَتِهِمُ المُشْرِكِينَ بِالدَّسِّ وتَلْقِينِ الشُّبَهِ؛ تَذْكِيرًا لَهم بِحالِ فِرْعَوْنَ وقَوْمِهِ إذْ قالَ لَهُ فِرْعَوْنُ ﴿إنِّي لَأظُنُّكَ يا مُوسى مَسْحُورًا﴾.

والخِطابُ في قَوْلِهِ ”فاسْألْ“ لِلنَّبِيِّ ﷺ، والمُرادُ: سُؤالُ الِاحْتِجاجِ بِهِمْ عَلى المُشْرِكِينَ، لا سُؤالُ الِاسْتِرْشادِ كَما هو بَيِّنٌ.

وقَوْلُهُ ”مَسْحُورًا“ ظاهِرُهُ أنَّ مَعْناهُ مُتَأثِّرًا بِالسِّحْرِ، أيْ سَحَرَكَ السَّحَرَةُ، وأفْسَدُوا عَقْلَكَ؛ فَصِرْتَ تَهْرِفُ بِالكَلامِ الباطِلِ الدّالِّ عَلى خَلَلِ العَقْلِ، مِثْلَ المَيْمُونِ والمَشْئُومِ. وهَذا قَوْلٌ قالَهُ فِرْعَوْنُ في مَقامٍ غَيْرِ الَّذِي قالَ لَهُ فِيهِ ﴿يُرِيدُ أنْ يُخْرِجَكم مِن أرْضِكم بِسِحْرِهِ﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 35]، والَّذِي قالَ فِيهِ ﴿إنَّ هَذا لَساحِرٌ عَلِيمٌ﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 34]، فَيَكُونُ إعْراضًا عَنِ الِاشْتِغالِ بِالآياتِ، وإقْبالًا عَلى تَطَلُّعِ حالِ مُوسى فِيما يَقُولُهُ مِن غَرائِبِ الأقْوالِ عِنْدَهم، ألا تَرى إلى قَوْلِهِ تَعالى حِكايَةً عَنْهُ ﴿قالَ لِمَن حَوْلَهُ ألا تَسْتَمِعُونَ﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 25]، وكُلُّ تِلْكَ الأقْوالِ صَدَرَتْ مِن فِرْعَوْنَ في مَقاماتِ مُحاوَراتِهِ مَعَ مُوسى عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ، فَحُكِيَ في كُلِّ آيَةٍ مِنها شَيْءٌ مِنها.

و(إذا) ظَرْفٌ مُتَعَلِّقٌ بِـ”آتَيْنا“، والضَّمِيرُ المَنصُوبُ في ”جاءَهم“ عائِدٌ إلى بَنِي إسْرائِيلَ، وأصْلُ الكَلامِ: ولَقَدْ آتَيْنا مُوسى تِسْعَ آياتٍ بَيِّناتٍ إذْ جاءَ بَنِي إسْرائِيلَ، فاسْألْهم.

وكانَ فِرْعَوْنُ تَعَلَّقَ ظَنُّهُ بِحَقِيقَةِ ما أظْهَرَ مِنَ الآياتِ، فَرَجَحَ عِنْدَهُ أنَّها سِحْرٌ، أوْ تَعَلَّقَ ظَنُّهُ بِحَقِيقَةِ حالِ مُوسى، فَرَجَحَ عِنْدَهُ أنَّهُ أصابَهُ سِحْرٌ؛ لِأنَّ الظَّنَّ دُونَ اليَقِينِ، قالَ تَعالى ﴿إنْ نَظُنُّ إلّا ظَنًّا وما نَحْنُ بِمُسْتَيْقِنِينَ﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 32]، وقَدْ يُسْتَعْمَلُ الظَّنُّ بِمَعْنى العِلْمِ اليَقِينِ.

ومَعْنى ﴿لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ ما أنْزَلَ هَؤُلاءِ إلّا رَبُّ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ﴾: أنَّ فِرْعَوْنَ لَمْ يَبْقَ في نَفْسِهِ شَكٌّ في أنَّ تِلْكَ الآياتِ لا تَكُونُ إلّا بِتَسْخِيرِ اللَّهِ، إذْ لا يَقْدِرُ عَلَيْها غَيْرُ اللَّهِ، وأنَّهُ إنَّما قالَ ﴿إنِّي لَأظُنُّكَ يا مُوسى مَسْحُورًا﴾ عِنادًا ومُكابَرَةً وكِبْرِياءَ.

[صفحة ٢٢٧]
وأُكِّدَ كَلامُ مُوسى بِلامِ القَسَمِ، وحَرْفِ التَّحْقِيقِ؛ تَحْقِيقًا لِحُصُولِ عِلْمِ فِرْعَوْنَ بِذَلِكَ. وإنَّما أيْقَنَ مُوسى بِأنَّ فِرْعَوْنَ قَدْ عَلِمَ بِذَلِكَ: إمّا بِوَحْيٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ أعْلَمَهُ بِهِ، وإمّا بِرَأْيٍ مُصِيبٍ؛ لِأنَّ حُصُولَ العِلْمِ عِنْدَ قِيامِ البُرْهانِ الضَّرُورِيِّ حُصُولٌ عَقْلِيٌّ طَبِيعِيٌّ، لا يَتَخَلَّفُ عَنْ عَقْلٍ سَلِيمٍ.

وقَرَأ الكِسائِيُّ وحْدَهُ ”لَقَدْ عَلِمْتُ“ بِضَمِّ التّاءِ، أيْ أنَّ تِلْكَ الآياتِ لَيْسَتْ بِسِحْرٍ - كَما زَعَمْتَ - كِنايَةً عَلى أنَّهُ واثِقٌ مِن نَفْسِهِ السَّلامَةَ مِنَ السِّحْرِ.

والإشارَةُ بِـ”هَؤُلاءِ“ إلى الآياتِ التِّسْعِ جِيءَ لَها بِاسْمِ إشارَةِ العاقِلِ، وهو اسْتِعْمالٌ مَشْهُورٌ، ومِنهُ قَوْلُهُ تَعالى ﴿إنَّ السَّمْعَ والبَصَرَ والفُؤادَ كُلُّ أُولَئِكَ كانَ عَنْهُ مَسْئُولًا﴾ [al-Isra': 36]، وقَوْلُ جَرِيرٍ:

ذُمَّ المَنازِلَ بَعْدَ مَنزِلَةِ اللَّوى ∗∗∗ والعَيْشَ بَعْدَ أُولَئِكَ الأيّامِ

(Blame the dwellings after the abode of al-Liwa, and the life after those days.)

والأكْثَرُ أنْ يُشارَ بِـ(أُولاءِ) إلى العاقِلِ.
والبَصائِرُ: الحُجَجُ المُفِيدَةُ لِلْبَصِيرَةِ، أيِ العِلْمِ، فَكَأنَّها نَفْسُ البَصِيرَةِ.

وقَدْ تَقَدَّمَ عِنْدَ قَوْلِهِ تَعالى ﴿هَذا بَصائِرُ مِن رَبِّكُمْ﴾ [al-A'raf: 203] في آخِرِ الأعْرافِ.

وعَبَّرَ عَنِ اللَّهِ بِطَرِيقِ إضافَةِ وصْفِ الرَّبِّ لِلسَّماواتِ والأرْضِ؛ تَذْكِيرًا بِأنَّ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ والأرْضَ هو القادِرُ عَلى أنْ يَخْلُقَ مِثْلَ هَذِهِ الخَوارِقِ.

والمَثْبُورُ: الَّذِي أصابَهُ الثُّبُورُ، وهو الهَلاكُ، وهَذا نِذارَةٌ وتَهْدِيدٌ لِفِرْعَوْنَ بِقُرْبِ هَلاكِهِ. وإنَّما جَعَلَهُ مُوسى ظَنًّا؛ تَأدُّبًا مَعَ اللَّهِ تَعالى، أوْ لِأنَّهُ عَلِمَ ذَلِكَ بِاسْتِقْراءٍ تامٍّ، أفادَهُ هَلاكُ المُعانِدِينَ لِلرُّسُلِ، ولَكِنَّهُ لَمْ يَدْرِ لَعَلَّ فِرْعَوْنَ يُقْلِعُ عَنْ ذَلِكَ، وكانَ عِنْدَهُ احْتِمالٌ ضَعِيفٌ، فَلِذَلِكَ جَعَلَ تَوَقُّعَ هَلاكِ فِرْعَوْنَ ظَنًّا. ويَجُوزُ أنْ يَكُونَ الظَّنُّ هُنا مُسْتَعْمَلًا بِمَعْنى اليَقِينِ كَما تَقَدَّمَ آنِفًا.

وفِي ذِكْرِ هَذا مِن قِصَّةِ مُوسى إتْمامٌ لِتَمْثِيلِ حالِ مُعانِدِي الرِّسالَةِ المُحَمَّدِيَّةِ بِحالِ مَن عانَدَ رِسالَةَ مُوسى عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ.

[صفحة ٢٢٨]
وجاءَ في جَوابِ مُوسى عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ لِفِرْعَوْنَ بِمِثْلِ ما شافَهَهُ فِرْعَوْنُ بِهِ مِن قَوْلِهِ ﴿إنِّي لَأظُنُّكَ يا مُوسى مَسْحُورًا﴾، مُقارَعَةً لَهُ، وإظْهارًا لِكَوْنِهِ لا يَخافُهُ، وأنَّهُ يُعامِلُهُ مُعامَلَةَ المِثْلِ، قالَ تَعالى ﴿فَمَنِ اعْتَدى عَلَيْكم فاعْتَدُوا عَلَيْهِ بِمِثْلِ ما اعْتَدى عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ [al-Baqarah: 194].

بَقِيَ قَوْلُهم ﴿أوْ تُسْقِطَ السَّماءَ كَما زَعَمْتَ عَلَيْنا كِسَفًا﴾ [al-Isra': 92] غَيْرَ مَرْدُودٍ عَلَيْهِمْ؛ لِأنَّ لَهُ مُخالَفَةً لِبَقِيَّةِ ما اقْتَرَحُوهُ بِأنَّهُ اقْتِراحُ آيَةِ عَذابٍ ورُعْبٍ، فَهو مِن قَبِيلِ آياتِ مُوسى عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ التِّسْعِ، فَكانَ ذِكْرُ ما آتاهُ اللَّهُ مُوسى مِنَ الآياتِ، وعَدَمِ إجْداءِ ذَلِكَ في فِرْعَوْنَ وقَوْمِهِ تَنْظِيرًا لِما سَألَهُ المُشْرِكُونَ.

وَالمَقْصُودُ: أنَّنا آتَيْنا مُوسى عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ تِسْعَ آياتٍ بَيِّناتِ الدَّلالَةِ عَلى صِدْقِهِ، فَلَمْ يَهْتَدِ فِرْعَوْنُ وقَوْمُهُ، وزَعَمُوا ذَلِكَ سِحْرًا، فَفي ذَلِكَ

[صفحة ٢٢٥]
مَثَلٌ لِلْمُكابِرِينَ كُلِّهِمْ، وما قُرَيْشٌ إلّا مِنهم، فَفي هَذا مَثَلٌ لِلْمُعانِدِينَ وتَسْلِيَةٌ لِلرَّسُولِ. والآياتُ التِّسْعُ هي: بَياضُ يَدِهِ كُلَّما أدْخَلَها في جَيْبِهِ وأخْرَجَها، وانْقِلابُ العَصا حَيَّةً، والطُّوفانُ، والجَرادُ، والقَمْلُ، والضَّفادِعُ، والدَّمُ، والرِّجْزُ وهو الدُّمَّلُ، والقَحْطُ وهو السُّنُونَ ونَقْصُ الثَّمَراتِ. وهي مَذْكُورَةٌ في سُورَةِ الأعْرافِ، وجَمَعَها الفَيْرُوزَ آبادِيُّ في قَوْلِهِ:

عَصًا سَنَةٌ بَحْرٌ جَرادٌ وقُمَّلُ يَدٌ ودَمٌ بَعْدَ الضَّفادِعِ طُوفانُ

(أي: العصا، والسنة [القحط]، والبحر [الماء]، والجراد، والقمل، واليد، والدم، ثم الضفادع، والطوفان.)

فَقَدْ حَصَلَتْ بِقَوْلِهِ ﴿ولَقَدْ آتَيْنا مُوسى تِسْعَ آياتٍ بَيِّناتٍ﴾ الحُجَّةُ عَلى المُشْرِكِينَ الَّذِينَ يَقْتَرِحُونَ الآياتِ.

ثُمَّ لَمْ يَزَلِ الِاعْتِناءُ في هَذِهِ السُّورَةِ بِالمُقارَنَةِ بَيْنَ رِسالَةِ مُحَمَّدٍ ﷺ، ورِسالَةِ مُوسى عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ، إقامَةً لِلْحُجَّةِ عَلى المُشْرِكِينَ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِالرِّسالَةِ بِعِلَّةِ أنَّ الَّذِي جاءَهم بَشَرٌ، ولِلْحُجَّةِ عَلى أهْلِ الكِتابِ الَّذِينَ ظاهَرُوا المُشْرِكِينَ، ولَقَّنُوهم شُبَهَ الإلْحادِ في الرِّسالَةِ المُحَمَّدِيَّةِ؛ لِيَصْفُوَ لَهم جَوُّ العِلْمِ في بِلادِ العَرَبِ، وهم ما كانُوا يَحْسُبُونَ لِما وراءَ ذَلِكَ حِسابًا.

فالمَعْنى: ولَقَدْ آتَيْنا مُوسى تِسْعَ آياتٍ عَلى رِسالَتِهِ.

وهَذا مِثْلُ التَّنْظِيرِ بَيْنَ إيتاءِ مُوسى، وإيتاءِ القُرْآنِ، في قَوْلِهِ في أوَّلِ السُّورَةِ ﴿وآتَيْنا مُوسى الكِتابَ﴾ [al-Isra': 2] الآياتِ، ثُمَّ قَوْلِهِ ﴿إنَّ هَذا القُرْآنَ يَهْدِي لِلَّتِي هي أقْوَمُ﴾ [al-Isra': 9].

فَتَكُونُ هَذِهِ الجُمْلَةُ عَطْفًا عَلى جُمْلَةِ ﴿قُلْ سُبْحانَ رَبِّي هَلْ كُنْتُ إلّا بَشَرًا رَسُولًا﴾ [al-Isra': 93] أوْ عَلى جُمْلَةِ ﴿قُلْ لَوْ أنْتُمْ تَمْلِكُونَ خَزائِنَ رَحْمَةِ رَبِّي﴾ [al-Isra': 100] الآيَةَ، ثُمَّ انْتَقَلَ مِن ذَلِكَ بِطَرِيقَةِ التَّفْرِيعِ إلى التَّسْجِيلِ بِبَنِي إسْرائِيلَ؛ اسْتِشْهادًا بِهِمْ عَلى المُشْرِكِينَ، وإدْماجًا لِلتَّعْرِيضِ بِهِمْ بِأنَّهم ساوَوُا المُشْرِكِينَ في إنْكارِ

[صفحة ٢٢٦]
نُبُوَّةِ مُحَمَّدٍ ﷺ، ومُظاهَرَتِهِمُ المُشْرِكِينَ بِالدَّسِّ وتَلْقِينِ الشُّبَهِ؛ تَذْكِيرًا لَهم بِحالِ فِرْعَوْنَ وقَوْمِهِ إذْ قالَ لَهُ فِرْعَوْنُ ﴿إنِّي لَأظُنُّكَ يا مُوسى مَسْحُورًا﴾.

والخِطابُ في قَوْلِهِ ”فاسْألْ“ لِلنَّبِيِّ ﷺ، والمُرادُ: سُؤالُ الِاحْتِجاجِ بِهِمْ عَلى المُشْرِكِينَ، لا سُؤالُ الِاسْتِرْشادِ كَما هو بَيِّنٌ.

وقَوْلُهُ ”مَسْحُورًا“ ظاهِرُهُ أنَّ مَعْناهُ مُتَأثِّرًا بِالسِّحْرِ، أيْ سَحَرَكَ السَّحَرَةُ، وأفْسَدُوا عَقْلَكَ؛ فَصِرْتَ تَهْرِفُ بِالكَلامِ الباطِلِ الدّالِّ عَلى خَلَلِ العَقْلِ، مِثْلَ المَيْمُونِ والمَشْئُومِ. وهَذا قَوْلٌ قالَهُ فِرْعَوْنُ في مَقامٍ غَيْرِ الَّذِي قالَ لَهُ فِيهِ ﴿يُرِيدُ أنْ يُخْرِجَكم مِن أرْضِكم بِسِحْرِهِ﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 35]، والَّذِي قالَ فِيهِ ﴿إنَّ هَذا لَساحِرٌ عَلِيمٌ﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 34]، فَيَكُونُ إعْراضًا عَنِ الِاشْتِغالِ بِالآياتِ، وإقْبالًا عَلى تَطَلُّعِ حالِ مُوسى فِيما يَقُولُهُ مِن غَرائِبِ الأقْوالِ عِنْدَهم، ألا تَرى إلى قَوْلِهِ تَعالى حِكايَةً عَنْهُ ﴿قالَ لِمَن حَوْلَهُ ألا تَسْتَمِعُونَ﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 25]، وكُلُّ تِلْكَ الأقْوالِ صَدَرَتْ مِن فِرْعَوْنَ في مَقاماتِ مُحاوَراتِهِ مَعَ مُوسى عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ، فَحُكِيَ في كُلِّ آيَةٍ مِنها شَيْءٌ مِنها.

و(إذا) ظَرْفٌ مُتَعَلِّقٌ بِـ”آتَيْنا“، والضَّمِيرُ المَنصُوبُ في ”جاءَهم“ عائِدٌ إلى بَنِي إسْرائِيلَ، وأصْلُ الكَلامِ: ولَقَدْ آتَيْنا مُوسى تِسْعَ آياتٍ بَيِّناتٍ إذْ جاءَ بَنِي إسْرائِيلَ، فاسْألْهم.

وكانَ فِرْعَوْنُ تَعَلَّقَ ظَنُّهُ بِحَقِيقَةِ ما أظْهَرَ مِنَ الآياتِ، فَرَجَحَ عِنْدَهُ أنَّها سِحْرٌ، أوْ تَعَلَّقَ ظَنُّهُ بِحَقِيقَةِ حالِ مُوسى، فَرَجَحَ عِنْدَهُ أنَّهُ أصابَهُ سِحْرٌ؛ لِأنَّ الظَّنَّ دُونَ اليَقِينِ، قالَ تَعالى ﴿إنْ نَظُنُّ إلّا ظَنًّا وما نَحْنُ بِمُسْتَيْقِنِينَ﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 32]، وقَدْ يُسْتَعْمَلُ الظَّنُّ بِمَعْنى العِلْمِ اليَقِينِ.

ومَعْنى ﴿لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ ما أنْزَلَ هَؤُلاءِ إلّا رَبُّ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ﴾: أنَّ فِرْعَوْنَ لَمْ يَبْقَ في نَفْسِهِ شَكٌّ في أنَّ تِلْكَ الآياتِ لا تَكُونُ إلّا بِتَسْخِيرِ اللَّهِ، إذْ لا يَقْدِرُ عَلَيْها غَيْرُ اللَّهِ، وأنَّهُ إنَّما قالَ ﴿إنِّي لَأظُنُّكَ يا مُوسى مَسْحُورًا﴾ عِنادًا ومُكابَرَةً وكِبْرِياءَ.

[صفحة ٢٢٧]
وأُكِّدَ كَلامُ مُوسى بِلامِ القَسَمِ، وحَرْفِ التَّحْقِيقِ؛ تَحْقِيقًا لِحُصُولِ عِلْمِ فِرْعَوْنَ بِذَلِكَ. وإنَّما أيْقَنَ مُوسى بِأنَّ فِرْعَوْنَ قَدْ عَلِمَ بِذَلِكَ: إمّا بِوَحْيٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ أعْلَمَهُ بِهِ، وإمّا بِرَأْيٍ مُصِيبٍ؛ لِأنَّ حُصُولَ العِلْمِ عِنْدَ قِيامِ البُرْهانِ الضَّرُورِيِّ حُصُولٌ عَقْلِيٌّ طَبِيعِيٌّ، لا يَتَخَلَّفُ عَنْ عَقْلٍ سَلِيمٍ.

وقَرَأ الكِسائِيُّ وحْدَهُ ”لَقَدْ عَلِمْتُ“ بِضَمِّ التّاءِ، أيْ أنَّ تِلْكَ الآياتِ لَيْسَتْ بِسِحْرٍ - كَما زَعَمْتَ - كِنايَةً عَلى أنَّهُ واثِقٌ مِن نَفْسِهِ السَّلامَةَ مِنَ السِّحْرِ.

والإشارَةُ بِـ”هَؤُلاءِ“ إلى الآياتِ التِّسْعِ جِيءَ لَها بِاسْمِ إشارَةِ العاقِلِ، وهو اسْتِعْمالٌ مَشْهُورٌ، ومِنهُ قَوْلُهُ تَعالى ﴿إنَّ السَّمْعَ والبَصَرَ والفُؤادَ كُلُّ أُولَئِكَ كانَ عَنْهُ مَسْئُولًا﴾ [al-Isra': 36]، وقَوْلُ جَرِيرٍ:

ذُمَّ المَنازِلَ بَعْدَ مَنزِلَةِ اللَّوى ∗∗∗ والعَيْشَ بَعْدَ أُولَئِكَ الأيّامِ

(Blame the dwellings after the abode of al-Liwa, and the life after those days.)

والأكْثَرُ أنْ يُشارَ بِـ(أُولاءِ) إلى العاقِلِ.
والبَصائِرُ: الحُجَجُ المُفِيدَةُ لِلْبَصِيرَةِ، أيِ العِلْمِ، فَكَأنَّها نَفْسُ البَصِيرَةِ.

وقَدْ تَقَدَّمَ عِنْدَ قَوْلِهِ تَعالى ﴿هَذا بَصائِرُ مِن رَبِّكُمْ﴾ [al-A'raf: 203] في آخِرِ الأعْرافِ.

وعَبَّرَ عَنِ اللَّهِ بِطَرِيقِ إضافَةِ وصْفِ الرَّبِّ لِلسَّماواتِ والأرْضِ؛ تَذْكِيرًا بِأنَّ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ والأرْضَ هو القادِرُ عَلى أنْ يَخْلُقَ مِثْلَ هَذِهِ الخَوارِقِ.

والمَثْبُورُ: الَّذِي أصابَهُ الثُّبُورُ، وهو الهَلاكُ، وهَذا نِذارَةٌ وتَهْدِيدٌ لِفِرْعَوْنَ بِقُرْبِ هَلاكِهِ. وإنَّما جَعَلَهُ مُوسى ظَنًّا؛ تَأدُّبًا مَعَ اللَّهِ تَعالى، أوْ لِأنَّهُ عَلِمَ ذَلِكَ بِاسْتِقْراءٍ تامٍّ، أفادَهُ هَلاكُ المُعانِدِينَ لِلرُّسُلِ، ولَكِنَّهُ لَمْ يَدْرِ لَعَلَّ فِرْعَوْنَ يُقْلِعُ عَنْ ذَلِكَ، وكانَ عِنْدَهُ احْتِمالٌ ضَعِيفٌ، فَلِذَلِكَ جَعَلَ تَوَقُّعَ هَلاكِ فِرْعَوْنَ ظَنًّا. ويَجُوزُ أنْ يَكُونَ الظَّنُّ هُنا مُسْتَعْمَلًا بِمَعْنى اليَقِينِ كَما تَقَدَّمَ آنِفًا.

وفِي ذِكْرِ هَذا مِن قِصَّةِ مُوسى إتْمامٌ لِتَمْثِيلِ حالِ مُعانِدِي الرِّسالَةِ المُحَمَّدِيَّةِ بِحالِ مَن عانَدَ رِسالَةَ مُوسى عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ.

[صفحة ٢٢٨]
وجاءَ في جَوابِ مُوسى عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ لِفِرْعَوْنَ بِمِثْلِ ما شافَهَهُ فِرْعَوْنُ بِهِ مِن قَوْلِهِ ﴿إنِّي لَأظُنُّكَ يا مُوسى مَسْحُورًا﴾، مُقارَعَةً لَهُ، وإظْهارًا لِكَوْنِهِ لا يَخافُهُ، وأنَّهُ يُعامِلُهُ مُعامَلَةَ المِثْلِ، قالَ تَعالى ﴿فَمَنِ اعْتَدى عَلَيْكم فاعْتَدُوا عَلَيْهِ بِمِثْلِ ما اعْتَدى عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ [al-Baqarah: 194].

Commentary of Ibn 'Ashur (al-Tahrir wa al-Tanwir) on surah 17, verses 103–104:

﴿So he intended to drive them out of the land, but We drowned him and those with him, all together.﴾ ﴿And We said after him to the Children of Israel: "Dwell in the land, and when the promise of the Hereafter comes, We will bring you forth as a mixed multitude."﴾

The story of the parable is completed with what contains an allusion to the representation of the two states, as a warning to the polytheists that the outcome of their scheming, plotting and attempts will be what befell the scheming and plotting of Pharaoh. Thus, following the representation of the two messages and the state of those to whom both were sent, he mentions the outcome of the state that was used as the example, as a warning to those who are represented by that same fate.

The polytheists had resolved to expel the Prophet ﷺ and the Muslims from Makkah. Their intention was thus represented by the intention of Pharaoh to expel Musa and the Children of Israel from Egypt. God, the Exalted, says: ﴿And indeed they almost incited you to slip from the land to expel you from it; and then they would not remain after you except for a little.﴾ [al-Isra: 76].

Al-istifzaz (incitement/driving out) means al-istikhfaf (making light of, provoking), and it is a metonymy for expulsion. It was mentioned earlier at His saying, ﴿And indeed they almost incited you to slip from the land﴾ [al-Isra: 76] in this surah.

What is meant by ﴿those with him﴾ is his soldiers who went out with him, following the Children of Israel.

The first land is the one previously known, which is the land of Egypt, and the second land is the land of al-Sham, which was promised to the Children of Israel by God's promise to Ibrahim (Abraham).

The promise of the Hereafter is what God promised to the creation through the tongues of the messengers, namely resurrection and gathering.

Al-lafif (a mixed multitude) refers to groups composed of mixed people of various kinds. The meaning is: We judged between them in this world by drowning the disbelievers and granting the believers dominion, and We will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection.

The meaning of ﴿We will bring you﴾ is: We will present you before Us. The implied sense is: We will bring you to Us.

Commentary of Ibn 'Ashur (al-Tahrir wa al-Tanwir) on surah 17, verse 105:

﴿And with the truth We sent it down, and with the truth it descended.﴾ This returns to the praise of the Qur'an, connected to His saying: ﴿And We have certainly diversified in this Qur'an for the people from every example, but most of the people refused except denial﴾ [al-Isra': 89]. Then, when He joined to it ﴿And they say, "We will not believe you"﴾ [al-Isra': 90] and what follows up to here, and the occasion of mentioning Pharaoh's denial of Musa, peace be upon him, allowed it, the discourse returned to praising the Qur'an for that occasion.

The Qur'an has been described with two great attributes, each of which contains great praise and a call to reflect upon them.

The verb "descend" (nuzul) is mentioned twice, and in each instance it has a complement of the same wording but a different meaning. He made the sending down by God of it [the Qur'an] dependent on it being "with the truth" (bi-l-haqq), so the meaning of "truth" here is the established truth in which there is no doubt and no falsehood. This is like His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿This is the Book, there is no doubt in it﴾ [al-Baqara: 2], and it is a rebuttal of the claim of the polytheists that the Qur'an is not revelation from God.

He made the descent of the Qur'an, i.e., its reaching the people, dependent on it being "with the truth," so the second "truth" means the opposite of falsehood, i.e., containing the truth by which the people's welfare and their success in this world and the Hereafter are sustained, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And say, "The truth has come and falsehood has vanished"﴾ [al-Isra': 81], and His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book with the truth, that you may judge between the people by what God has shown you﴾ [al-Nisa': 105].

The pronouns of absence (ghayba) refer to the Qur'an, which is known from the context.

The bā' in both places is for accompaniment (al-musahaba), because it [the Qur'an] contains truth and guidance. Accompaniment resembles the adverbial sense of place (al-zarfiyya). Were it not for the difference in meaning of the two bā's in the verse, His saying ﴿and with the truth it descended﴾ would be merely an emphasis of His saying ﴿and with the truth We sent it down﴾, because when it was sent down with the truth, it descended with it. One should not resort to this unless no other meaning is determined.

The placement of the prepositional phrase before its governing verb in both places is for restriction (al-qasr), as a rebuttal of those who denied it, who claimed that it is "tales of the ancients," or "manifest magic," or something similar.

* * *

﴿And We did not send you except as a bringer of good news and a warner﴾

This is a parenthetical clause between the clause ﴿And with the truth We sent it down﴾ and the clause ﴿and [it is] a Qur'an that We have divided﴾ [al-Isra': 106], meaning: and in that truth there is benefit and harm; so you, with it, are a bringer of good news to the believers and a warner to the disbelievers.

The restriction is a rebuttal of those who asked him for things from the acts of God, Exalted is He, and of those who thought that the Messenger should not be a human being.

ۛ﴿And an Qur'an We have divided (into parts), that you may recite it to the people at intervals, and We have sent it down in stages﴾ is an continuation of the clause "We sent it down."

"Qur'an" is in the accusative as a state (ḥāl) of the pronoun object in "faraqnāhu," placed before its referent for emphasis (tanwīh) on the fact that it is a Qur'an, meaning that it is a book to be read. The name "Qur'an" is derived from qirā'a (recitation), which is tilāwa, indicating that it belongs to the category of speech that is memorized and recited, as indicated by His saying, ﴿These are the verses of the Book and a clear Qur'an﴾ [al-Ḥijr: 1], which has already been explained. This Book has names according to its attributes: it is a Book (kitāb), a Qur'an, a Furqan (criterion), a Reminder (dhikr), and a Revelation (tanzīl). The attributes apply to it, or some of them, according to the context. Do you not see His saying, ﴿and the Qur'an of dawn﴾ [al-Isrā': 78], and His saying, ﴿So recite what is easy of the Qur'an﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 20], considering that the context is the command to recite in prayer or in general, and His saying, ﴿Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His servant, that he may be a warner to the worlds﴾ [al-Furqan: 1], in the context of it being a discriminator between truth and falsehood. For this reason, none of the heavenly Books is described with the attribute "Qur'an" except the Book sent down upon Muḥammad (ﷺ).

The meaning of "faraqnāhu" is that We made it into separated parts, that is, We sent it down in portions, divided and not gathered into one heap (ṣabra). It is said: "farraqa al-ashyā'" when he separated things from each other, and "farraqa al-ṣabra" when he divided the heap into parts. The term "farq" is also applied to clarification (bayān), because clarification resembles separating mixed things; thus "faraqnāhu" may carry the meaning of "We clarified it and detailed it." Since "Qur'an" as a state of the pronoun in "faraqnāhu" leads the meaning to: We divided it and made it readable.

It has been given a reason by His saying, ﴿that you may recite it to the people at intervals﴾, so these are two causes: that it be recited to the people, and this is the cause of making it a Qur'an; and that it be recited at intervals, that is, with leisure and slowness, and this is the cause of its being divided.

The wisdom in this is that its words and meanings be more firmly established in the souls of the listeners.

The clause ﴿and We have sent it down in stages﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿And an Qur'an We have divided﴾. The doubling of the verb "nazzalnāhu" and its emphasis by the absolute object indicates the division of its descent mentioned in His saying, ﴿And with the truth We sent it down﴾ [al-Isrā': 105].

The explanation of the wisdom has been omitted, being sufficed by what is in His saying, ﴿that you may recite it to the people at intervals﴾, from the unity of the wisdom, which His saying, ﴿Thus, that We may strengthen your heart thereby, and We have arranged it in measured arrangement﴾ [al-Furqan: 32] explicitly states.

It is also possible that what is meant is: We divided its sending down, observing the causes and events. In both interpretations there is a refutation of their objection when they said, ﴿Why was the Qur'an not sent down to him all at once?﴾ [al-Furqan: 32].

Commentary of Ibn 'Ashur (al-Tahrir wa al-Tanwir) on surah 17, verses 107–109:

Page 232
﴿Say, "Believe in it or do not believe. Indeed, those who were given knowledge before it, when it is recited to them, fall upon their faces in prostration,﴾ ﴿and say, "Glory be to our Lord! Indeed, the promise of our Lord has been fulfilled."﴾ ﴿And they fall upon their faces weeping, and it increases them in humility.﴾

This is a resumption of address to the Prophet (ﷺ), to instruct him in what he should say to the polytheists who do not believe that the Qur'an is sent down from Allah. After He had clarified for them the proofs that such a Qur'an could only be sent down from Allah, from His saying ﴿Say, "If mankind and the jinn gathered together to produce the like of this Qur'an, they would not produce its like"﴾ [al-Isra: 88], so they were unable to produce its like; then (He clarified) the virtues of what it comprises, with His saying ﴿And We have certainly displayed for the people in this Qur'an from every example﴾ [al-Isra: 89]; then by alluding to what they proposed regarding bringing other miracles; then He uncovers their doubt with which they disguise their refusal to believe in the messengership of a human being, and clarifies for them their error or their sophistry; then by commanding (the Prophet) to take Allah as witness between him and them; then by threatening them with the punishment of the Hereafter; then by portraying their situation with their Messenger by the situation of Pharaoh and his people with Moses, and what was hastened for them of the punishment of this world by annihilation; then by uncovering their doubt concerning the gradual revelation of the Qur'an, He followed that by leaving to them the consideration of preferring belief in the truth of the Qur'an or non-belief, with His saying ﴿Believe in it or do not believe﴾, meaning equality between their belief and their non-belief in the sight of Allah, the Exalted. So the imperative in His saying "Believe" (āminū) is for equalization, i.e., "if you wish."

"Do not believe" (lā tu'minū) is in the jussive mood by coordination with the jussive form preceding it, and similar to it is His saying in Surat al-Tur ﴿Be patient or be not patient; it is the same for you﴾ [al-Tur: 16]. The particle (lā) is a particle of negation, not a particle of prohibition, and it does not occur with an imperative meant to express equalization except in this way. It is a metaphor (kināya) for turning away from them, disdaining them, and paying them little regard, and along with that it includes consolation for the Messenger (ﷺ).

Page 233
The clause ﴿Indeed, those who were given knowledge﴾ serves as a causal justification for the meaning of equalization between their belief in it and their non-belief, or as a causal justification for the verb "Say," or for both, in the manner of causes that come after several clauses; for this reason it is separated (without a conjunction). The position of (inna) here is the position of the resultative fā' (the fā' of consequence), meaning: your belief in the Qur'an and your non-belief are only equal, because it is independent of your belief through the belief of those who were given knowledge before its revelation. They are more superior to you in intellect and more excellent in standing, and they are those who were given knowledge; for they hear it, and believe in it, and it increases them in faith through what is in their books of the promise of the Messenger by whom this was sent down.

In this there is an allusion that those who turned away from belief in the Qur'an are ignorant, and people of ignorance (jāhiliyya).

By "those who were given knowledge" is meant the likes of Waraqa ibn Nawfal, for the people of Makkah had heard of his testimony to the Prophet (ﷺ), and those who believed after the revelation of this surah, such as 'Abd Allah ibn Salam, Mu'ayqib, and Salman al-Farisi.

So in this verse there is a report of the unseen.

The pronouns in (bihi, min qablihi, yutlā) refer to the Qur'an, and the speech is by the omission of a known genitive (muḍāf) which is understood from the context and is customary to omit, i.e., "believe in its truth," and "before its revelation."

Al-khurūr: the falling of the body. Allah, the Exalted, said ﴿So the roof fell upon them from above them﴾ [al-Nahl: 26].

It has already been discussed in His saying ﴿And Moses fell down unconscious﴾ [al-A'raf: 143] in Surat al-A'raf.

The lām in "li-l-adhqān" is in the sense of "ʿalā" (upon), as in the saying of Allah, the Exalted, ﴿And He threw him down upon his forehead﴾ [al-Saffat: 103], and the saying of Ta'abbaṭa Sharran:

"Prostrate upon both hands and upon the cheeks"

Page 234
The original basis of this lām is that it is a subsequent metaphor (isti'āra tab'iyya): the particle of specification (ikhtiṣāṣ) has been borrowed for the meaning of elevation (isti'lā'), to indicate greater firmness, like the firmness of a thing with what is specific to it.
Al-adhqān is the plural of al-dhaqan (with a fatha on the dhāl and a fatha on the qāf), the meeting place of the two jaws. He mentioned the chin to indicate their placing all their faces upon the ground, out of the strength of their desire to prostrate, because in it is the evocation of humility before Allah, the Exalted.

"Sujjadan" is the plural of sājid, and it is in the position of a circumstantial accusative (ḥāl) from the pronoun in "yakharrūna," to clarify the purpose of this falling; and their prostration is the prostration of glorification of Allah when they witness a sign from the proofs of His knowledge and the truthfulness of His messengers, and the realization of His promise.

"Wa-yaqūlūna subḥāna rabbinā" is coordinated upon "yakharrūna," to indicate that they combine the act that signifies submission with the speech that signifies transcendence and glorification. A parallel to it is His saying ﴿They fell down in prostration and glorified the praise of their Lord﴾ [al-Sajda: 15]. Moreover, in their saying ﴿Glory be to our Lord﴾ there is an indication of wonder and delight at the fulfillment of Allah's promise in the Torah and the Gospel regarding the coming of the final Messenger (ﷺ).

The clause ﴿If the promise of our Lord was certainly to be fulfilled﴾ is part of their speech, and it is the intended purpose of the saying; because their glorification before it is glorification of wonder and reflection that it is the Book promised, and of His Messenger in the previous scriptures.

"In" (إنْ) is a lightened form of the heavy (inna), and its operation has been nullified because of the lightening, and a verb followed it, from among the abrogators of the subject, following the usual usage of the lightened form; and the predicate of the abrogator was connected with the lām that distinguishes the lightened from the negating (in).

"Al-wa'd" (the promise) remains on its original basis of being a verbal noun (maṣdariyya), and the realization of the promise necessitates the realization of what was promised; so the confirmation of the promise and of what was promised is achieved.

The meaning of "mafʿūlan" is that Allah does what came in His promise, i.e., brings it into existence and realizes it; and this prostration is a prostration of glorification of Allah, since He fulfilled His promise after long years.

Page 235
His saying ﴿And they fall upon their faces weeping﴾ is a repetition of the clause with a difference in the accompanying circumstance; the clause is repeated as a preparation for mentioning the circumstance, and repetition may occur with coordination because of the difference in qualifiers, so that difference is what justifies the coordination, as in the saying of Murra ibn 'Adda al-Faqʿasi:

"Why did they not count me for one like me, when they lost one another, when the opponent is bent, his head inclined, and his nose bent down?"

"Why did they not count me for one like me, when they lost one another, while in the earth there is one firmly established, a brave man, and a scorpion?"

The falling narrated by the second clause is the first falling; they fell only once, in prostration and weeping, and it was mentioned twice out of concern for what accompanied it of signs of humility.

"Yabkūn" is mentioned in the present form to bring the state to mind.

The weeping is weeping of joy and delight; and weeping arises from an inward emotion originating from sorrow, or from fear, or from longing.

And the Qur'an increases them in humility over the humility they already had from hearing their Book.

From the Sunnah is the prostration of the reciter and the listener to it, with the intention of this verse, following those prostrating ones, such that a Muslim, whenever he mentions the prostration of the People of the Book upon hearing the Qur'an, sees himself as more deserving of prostration when reciting the Qur'an.

In this there is an allusion that those who turned away from belief in the Qur'an are ignorant, and people of ignorance (jāhiliyya).

By "those who were given knowledge" is meant the likes of Waraqa ibn Nawfal, for the people of Makkah had heard of his testimony to the Prophet (ﷺ), and those who believed after the revelation of this surah, such as 'Abd Allah ibn Salam, Mu'ayqib, and Salman al-Farisi.

So in this verse there is a report of the unseen.

The pronouns in (bihi, min qablihi, yutlā) refer to the Qur'an, and the speech is by the omission of a known genitive (muḍāf) which is understood from the context and is customary to omit, i.e., "believe in its truth," and "before its revelation."

Al-khurūr: the falling of the body. Allah, the Exalted, said ﴿So the roof fell upon them from above them﴾ [al-Nahl: 26].

It has already been discussed in His saying ﴿And Moses fell down unconscious﴾ [al-A'raf: 143] in Surat al-A'raf.

The lām in "li-l-adhqān" is in the sense of "ʿalā" (upon), as in the saying of Allah, the Exalted, ﴿And He threw him down upon his forehead﴾ [al-Saffat: 103], and the saying of Ta'abbaṭa Sharran:

"Prostrate upon both hands and upon the cheeks"

Page 234
The original basis of this lām is that it is a subsequent metaphor (isti'āra tab'iyya): the particle of specification (ikhtiṣāṣ) has been borrowed for the meaning of elevation (isti'lā'), to indicate greater firmness, like the firmness of a thing with what is specific to it.
Al-adhqān is the plural of al-dhaqan (with a fatha on the dhāl and a fatha on the qāf), the meeting place of the two jaws. He mentioned the chin to indicate their placing all their faces upon the ground, out of the strength of their desire to prostrate, because in it is the evocation of humility before Allah, the Exalted.

"Sujjadan" is the plural of sājid, and it is in the position of a circumstantial accusative (ḥāl) from the pronoun in "yakharrūna," to clarify the purpose of this falling; and their prostration is the prostration of glorification of Allah when they witness a sign from the proofs of His knowledge and the truthfulness of His messengers, and the realization of His promise.

"Wa-yaqūlūna subḥāna rabbinā" is coordinated upon "yakharrūna," to indicate that they combine the act that signifies submission with the speech that signifies transcendence and glorification. A parallel to it is His saying ﴿They fell down in prostration and glorified the praise of their Lord﴾ [al-Sajda: 15]. Moreover, in their saying ﴿Glory be to our Lord﴾ there is an indication of wonder and delight at the fulfillment of Allah's promise in the Torah and the Gospel regarding the coming of the final Messenger (ﷺ).

The clause ﴿If the promise of our Lord was certainly to be fulfilled﴾ is part of their speech, and it is the intended purpose of the saying; because their glorification before it is glorification of wonder and reflection that it is the Book promised, and of His Messenger in the previous scriptures.

"In" (إنْ) is a lightened form of the heavy (inna), and its operation has been nullified because of the lightening, and a verb followed it, from among the abrogators of the subject, following the usual usage of the lightened form; and the predicate of the abrogator was connected with the lām that distinguishes the lightened from the negating (in).

"Al-wa'd" (the promise) remains on its original basis of being a verbal noun (maṣdariyya), and the realization of the promise necessitates the realization of what was promised; so the confirmation of the promise and of what was promised is achieved.

The meaning of "mafʿūlan" is that Allah does what came in His promise, i.e., brings it into existence and realizes it; and this prostration is a prostration of glorification of Allah, since He fulfilled His promise after long years.

Page 235
His saying ﴿And they fall upon their faces weeping﴾ is a repetition of the clause with a difference in the accompanying circumstance; the clause is repeated as a preparation for mentioning the circumstance, and repetition may occur with coordination because of the difference in qualifiers, so that difference is what justifies the coordination, as in the saying of Murra ibn 'Adda al-Faqʿasi:

"Why did they not count me for one like me, when they lost one another, when the opponent is bent, his head inclined, and his nose bent down?"

"Why did they not count me for one like me, when they lost one another, while in the earth there is one firmly established, a brave man, and a scorpion?"

The falling narrated by the second clause is the first falling; they fell only once, in prostration and weeping, and it was mentioned twice out of concern for what accompanied it of signs of humility.

"Yabkūn" is mentioned in the present form to bring the state to mind.

The weeping is weeping of joy and delight; and weeping arises from an inward emotion originating from sorrow, or from fear, or from longing.

And the Qur'an increases them in humility over the humility they already had from hearing their Book.

From the Sunnah is the prostration of the reciter and the listener to it, with the intention of this verse, following those prostrating ones, such that a Muslim, whenever he mentions the prostration of the People of the Book upon hearing the Qur'an, sees himself as more deserving of prostration when reciting the Qur'an.

Commentary of Ibn 'Ashur (al-Tahrir wa al-Tanwir) on surah 17, verses 107–109:

Indeed, the promise of our Lord has been fulfilled."﴾ ﴿And they fall upon their faces weeping, and it increases them in humility.﴾

This is a resumption of address to the Prophet (ﷺ), to instruct him in what he should say to the polytheists who do not believe that the Qur'an is sent down from Allah. After He had clarified for them the proofs that such a Qur'an could only be sent down from Allah, from His saying ﴿Say, "If mankind and the jinn gathered together to produce the like of this Qur'an, they would not produce its like"﴾ [al-Isra: 88], so they were unable to produce its like; then (He clarified) the virtues of what it comprises, with His saying ﴿And We have certainly displayed for the people in this Qur'an from every example﴾ [al-Isra: 89]; then by alluding to what they proposed regarding bringing other miracles; then He uncovers their doubt with which they disguise their refusal to believe in the messengership of a human being, and clarifies for them their error or their sophistry; then by commanding (the Prophet) to take Allah as witness between him and them; then by threatening them with the punishment of the Hereafter; then by portraying their situation with their Messenger by the situation of Pharaoh and his people with Moses, and what was hastened for them of the punishment of this world by annihilation; then by uncovering their doubt concerning the gradual revelation of the Qur'an, He followed that by leaving to them the consideration of preferring belief in the truth of the Qur'an or non-belief, with His saying ﴿Believe in it or do not believe﴾, meaning equality between their belief and their non-belief in the sight of Allah, the Exalted. So the imperative in His saying "Believe" (āminū) is for equalization, i.e., "if you wish."

"Do not believe" (lā tu'minū) is in the jussive mood by coordination with the jussive form preceding it, and similar to it is His saying in Surat al-Tur ﴿Be patient or be not patient; it is the same for you﴾ [al-Tur: 16]. The particle (lā) is a particle of negation, not a particle of prohibition, and it does not occur with an imperative meant to express equalization except in this way. It is a metaphor (kināya) for turning away from them, disdaining them, and paying them little regard, and along with that it includes consolation for the Messenger (ﷺ).
